newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: RUGBY UNION-TRY OF THE TOUR LIFTS LIONS TO VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TRY OF THE TOUR LIFTS LIONS TO VICTORY.

text.p: Two moments of individual brilliance put the British Lions tour of South Africa back on track as they beat the Gauteng Lions 20-14 at Ellis Park on Wednesday.

Following Saturday's 35-30 defeat to Northern Transvaal, tries from scrum-half Austin Healey and John Bentley within a four-minute span in the second half allowed the tourists to shrug off a lacklustre first-half display and recapture the winning habit.

Healey's try in the 60th minute, converted by replacement full-back Neil Jenkins, put the Lions in front for the first time at 10-9 and Bentley then ran 60 metres for one of the finest tries ever scored by a Lion in South Africa.

The Lions trailed 9-3 at half-time due to a poor kicking performance from Mike Catt who succeeded with only one kick from six attempts while Gauteng's Dawie du Toit slotted three penalties from four attempts during the same period.

But the arrival of Jenkins for Tony Underwood in the 55th minute galvanised the Lions. With the forwards finally putting together a concerted drive upfield, the ball eventually came to Healey and the livewire scrum-half left du Toit for dead with a devstating sidestep.
Bentley then received a long pass from Jenkins inside the Lions half and weaved his way past almost half the Gauteng side to score under the posts.
Gauteng came back with an injury-time try from flanker Andre Vos, but it was no more than a consolation.

Lions captain Tim Rodber blamed a wet ball for a game often undermined by knock-ons and indiscipline. Two Gauteng players were warned for dangerous play, but referee Tappe Henning generally kept the lid on a match which simmered but, the Lions tries apart, never caught fire.

Gauteng Lions - 15-Dawie du Toit; 14-Joe Gillingham, 13-Jannie van der Walt, 12-Hennie Le Roux, 11-Pieter Hendriks; 10-Louis van Rensburg, 9-Johan Roux; 8-Warren Brosnihan, 7-Piet Krause, 6-Andre Vos, 5-Bruce Thorne, 4-Kobus Wiese (captain), 3-Kapstokvan Greuning, 2-Chris Rossouw (James Dalton 53 mins), 1-Roberto Grau (Balie Swart 62 mins).

British Lions - 15-Nick Beal; 14-John Bentley, 13-Jeremy Guscott, 12-Will Greenwood, 11-Tony Underwood (Neil Jenkins 54 mins); 10-Mike Catt, 9-Austin Healey; 8-Tim Rodber (captain), 7-Neil Back, 6-Rob Wainwright, 5-Jeremy Davidson, 4-Nigel Redman, 3-Paul Wallace, 2-Barry Williams, 1-Tom Smith.
